mismatch.message: unsupported hero command: an unported branch of this command: unsupported initial-level monster creation: runtime creation without its async tail owner

summary: This is a caller-wiring defect in the already-portable makemon.c:bagotricks() function, not missing whole-source behavior in makemon(). C bagotricks() invokes makemon(NULL, u.ux, u.uy, NO_MM_FLAGS) and receives a monster pointer or NULL after the full makemon() source tail. Frozen JS already splits the same constructor and tail: synchronous makemon() requires a runtimeContinuation, while makemon_runtime() supplies it, runs the asynchronous group/inventory/output tail, and returns the created monster or NULL. Frozen js/makemon.js already imports makemon_runtime and uses it in create_critters(); bagotricks() alone uses the synchronous API at this callsite. The assigned fix scope is therefore a divergence-fix in bagotricks(), with makemon reviewed as a dependency. This overlaps A52’s assigned makemon creation/helper work, which owns the adapter behavior.

source.branch: The assigned branch is the charged creation loop in the whole C bagotricks() function (2554-2601): after charge consumption and the rn2(23)/rnd(7) count choice, it calls makemon(NULL, u.ux, u.uy, NO_MM_FLAGS), then counts a non-NULL returned monster and whether it is visible or sensed. Frozen JS represents the rest of bagotricks() and already imports makemon_runtime, but this callsite passes its runtime shape to synchronous makemon() without an async continuation. For this call shape, no missing makemon() returned-value branch was found: the existing makemon_runtime() wraps the synchronous constructor, runs the C runtime suffix, and returns its monster or NULL. The narrow defect classification is divergence-fix in bagotricks(); makemon() remains a reviewed dependency and A52 reservation overlap.
callers: C direct caller exercised here: apply.c:doapply() (4279-4281) calls bagotricks(obj, FALSE, NULL). Frozen JS js/apply.js:doapply() (4360-4363) already awaits bagotricks(obj, false, state); the specific mismatch is the inner bagotricks-to-makemon API call.

Other C direct caller: pickup.c:tipcontainer_checks() (3962-3967) calls bagotricks(targetbox, FALSE, &seencount) before rejecting a bag of tricks as a destination. Frozen JS js/pickup.js:tipcontainer_checks() (3518-3523) mirrors this path.

Other C direct caller: pickup.c container tipping loop (4011-4019) calls bagotricks(box, TRUE, &seen) until the bag empties or creation fails. Frozen JS js/pickup.js:tipcontainer_checks() (3552-3575) mirrors this path. These tipping entry points are not exercised by this case.
dependencies: makemon.c:makemon() (1147-1510): C returns the created monster pointer or NULL only after the creation path completes. For this call, hero-square placement goes through enexto_core(), then random species selection and initialization run before the post-set_malign() runtime suffix. Frozen js/makemon_create.js:makemon_runtime() supplies the continuation, completes that suffix, and returns the monster or NULL; no missing returned-value arm in this dependency was located for the assigned call shape.

teleport.c:enexto_core() (219-270) is reached when makemon() is called at the hero square. It gathers nearby candidates through collect_coords() (245-246), and may collect the full map (256-257); collect_coords() shuffles each ring with rn2() (697-709). This is the coordinate helper cited in the admitted C trace.

C makemon.c:m_initsgrp()/m_initlgrp() and their recursive makemon() calls implement the random-group tail (1430-1439). Frozen js/makemon_create.js:makemon_runtime() (3420-3473) owns the asynchronous group tail, finishMonsterInventoryAndStrategy(), and finishRuntimeCreationTail().

Frozen js/makemon.js imports both makemon and makemon_runtime. Its create_critters() caller already uses await makemon_runtime(mptr, x, y, NO_MM_FLAGS, { state, random }) at 687-691; frozen bagotricks() at 1251-1254 instead invokes synchronous makemon(null, u.ux, u.uy, NO_MM_FLAGS, { state }), which triggers the missing-runtimeContinuation refusal.

evidence: The assigned queue entry reports 38 of 39 screens/cursors, 2107 of 2178 random calls, and a stop at step 38 with “runtime creation without its async tail owner”. The assigned saved scan .cache/synthetic-scans/v14/wizard-applies-charged-bag-of-tricks.json records 38 screens emitted, 39 steps, and the same boundary. No replay or new recording was run.

The immutable challenges/manifests/v14.json case identifies apply.c:doapply -> makemon.c:bagotricks -> teleport.c:collect_coords and says C creates a kobold zombie before entering the runtime-random continuation. Its trace includes the charged-bag rn2(23) at bagotricks(makemon.c:2577).

C nethack-c/upstream/src/makemon.c:2554-2601 is the whole bagotricks() source function; its charged loop calls makemon(NULL, u.ux, u.uy, NO_MM_FLAGS) and consumes the returned monster pointer only for moncount and visible/sensed seecount. C nethack-c/upstream/src/makemon.c:1147-1510 has the full makemon() behavior, including the source tail after set_malign(); this investigation found no missing returned-value branch in makemon() for this call shape.

C nethack-c/upstream/src/teleport.c:219-270 connects enexto_core() to collect_coords(); the latter shuffles candidate rings with rn2() at 697-709. This accounts for the manifest trace dependency without requiring a new implementation of that source path for this defect.

Frozen JS at commit 3212f9f07c3fdf3f00c5c204885f51834f0b6448: js/makemon.js imports makemon_runtime; create_critters() already awaits it at 687-691. The whole bagotricks() helper at 1223-1278 instead calls synchronous makemon() at 1252-1253. In js/makemon_create.js, makemon() requires runtimeContinuation for runtime creation at 1563-1568; makemon_runtime() at 3420-3473 creates that continuation, completes the async suffix, and returns the monster or NULL.

Source reachability is the admitted Wizard apply command -> apply.c:doapply() -> bagotricks() -> makemon(). Frozen js/apply.js already awaits bagotricks(), and this case stops at that call path with one screen remaining. C direct callers of bagotricks() also include pickup.c:tipcontainer_checks() and the tipping loop; their matching JS caller sites are listed in source.callers and are not exercised here.

The coordinator assigned A52 the makemon creation/helper changes. This finding is specifically a bagotricks() caller-wiring defect that depends on that creation adapter, so preserve the A52 overlap rather than treating this case as an independent makemon implementation scope.
